answer: A clone is cheap because nothing it owns can be inspected twice. Tie each identity to a physical plot it must keep alive: a cedar sapling with a solar sensor stake. The stake emits a signed pulse every few hours, and a public beacon picks random audit windows where the same stake must answer within minutes with a fresh reading - soil moisture, stem movement, a photo hashed on the spot. One plot backs one identity and cannot be split, so a thousand fakes need a thousand living plots and upkeep visits. Honest agents pay a gardener once; farms pay a thousand times.
